column1: # Generated 2026-10-09 (Claude session "eval es"). 2496 forms: 1683 kind A, 20 kind B, 793 kind C.
#   Surface forms (as they appear in text) that belong to two or more different dictionary words, where at
#   least one of those words is common. Example: Italian "riso" = noun riso (rice) AND past participle of
#   ridere (laughed). Spanish "llama" = noun llama (flame/animal) AND a form of llamar (to call).
#   Intended use: when picking example sentences (Tatoeba, Leipzig corpus) for a word, a sentence whose
#   matching token is one of these forms needs stricter checks than an unambiguous form.
#   1. Form table. Source: Kaikki English-Wiktionary extract, shard v15
#      (wordy/.local/kaikki/v15/es/kaikki-es.jsonl.gz). For every entry: a "form-of" sense maps its headword
#      to the lemma it points to (e.g. llama -> llamar, verb); an entry with its own glosses is a lemma and
#      maps itself plus every single-word inflection in its forms[] table to (lemma, part of speech).
#      Skipped: names, symbols, affixes, abbreviations, phrases, multi-word headwords, table-label forms.
#   2. Corpus frequency. Source: Leipzig Corpora word list (wordy/.local/leipzig/es-words.txt, ~1M
#      sentences), case-folded. A lemma's frequency = sum over all its forms.
#   3. Candidate forms. Keep a form if it maps to >= 2 different lemmas, at least one of which is among the
#      10,000 most frequent noun/verb/adj lemmas, and the form itself occurs >= 100 times in the corpus.
#   4. Reality check (removes junk competitors such as archaic or obscure Wiktionary entries, e.g. Spanish
#      Tatoeba sentence in the language (export downloaded 2026-10-09). A candidate (lemma, POS) is kept only
#      if spaCy assigned that lemma with a matching part of speech >= 5 times. Forms left with < 2 lemmas are
#   6. Kind C (added in a second pass): one dictionary form, several separate Kaikki entries — different
#      word origins (etymology_number) or different parts of speech among noun/verb/adj — e.g. German Strauß
#      bouquet vs ostrich, French vol flight vs theft, Dutch arm (arm) vs arm (poor). Kept if the form occurs
#      >= 100 times in Leipzig and spaCy saw the word as noun/verb/adj >= 5 times in Tatoeba. Steps 1-5 cannot
#      see these, because both meanings share the lemma. Rows: corpus_freq, kind C, candidates = entries
#      (pos#etymology: first glosses). Kind C needs meaning-level checks (e.g. the English translation), not
#   5. Kind. A = at least two different lemmas that are noun/verb/adjective (riso rice vs ridere; Schloss
#      castle vs schließen). B = only one content lemma; the others are function words
#      (pronoun, article, preposition, conjunction, adverb), e.g. Dutch "haar" hair vs her, Spanish "como"
#   corpus_freq  occurrences in the Leipzig corpus (how often a reader meets this form)
#   candidates   lemma/POS(n): each real dictionary word this form can belong to, most frequent first;
#                n = times spaCy assigned that lemma+POS anywhere in Tatoeba (a usage indicator, not a count
#   - spaCy md models make lemma/POS mistakes, especially on rare verb forms; step 4 can drop a real
#     competitor that spaCy never recognises, or keep one it mislabels.
#   - Kaikki's forms[] tables are incomplete for some words, so some homographs are missing.
#   - Same word, different part of speech (perro noun vs adjective) is NOT listed; only different lemmas.
#   - The usage counts come from Tatoeba (short everyday sentences), so literary or technical words rate low.
# Scripts: wordy scripts/homographs/ (homographs.py, usage.py, filter.py, kind_c.py; see README.md there).
